primary.body:
## **User description** ## Summary Fixes issue #338 items 3 and 4: the encryption-migration-vs-protected-write race that CodeRabbit and Qodo both independently flagged on #337. - `assertNoActiveEncryptionMigration()` was a standalone read — a migration could claim ownership and commit in the gap between a protected writer's key resolution and its transaction commit, landing ciphertext under a superseded key/generation. - The same class of race let cache eviction / scene-revision retention delete records concurrently with a migration's verify pass, producing a false `ProtectedStoreVerificationShortfallError`. ## What changed - New `services/storage/protectedWriteAdmission.ts`: a Web Locks API (`navigator.locks`) shared/exclusive reader-writer lock. Ordinary protected writers hold it in shared mode for their full key-resolution-through-transaction-commit span; a migration batch holds it exclusively for one batch (~25 records), not the whole run — bounding writer starvation while closing the race exactly where it matters. - Wrapped every protected writer: `idbAssetStore.ts` (`saveImage`, `saveBinderAsset`, `deleteAllBinderAssetsForProject`, `deleteImage`, `deleteBinderAsset`), `idbCodexStore.ts` (`saveStoryCodex`, `saveRagVectors`, `deleteStoryCodex`), `idbProjectStore.ts` (`saveSlice`, `deleteProject`), `idbSnapshotStore.ts` (`createSnapshot`, `deleteSnapshot`). - Wrapped `protectedStoreMigration.ts`'s per-batch `adapter.migrateNext(...)` call in the exclusive variant. - Reused the same shared-mode wrapper at the two non-authoritative deletion sites (`aiInferenceCacheService.ts`'s durable-write section, `sceneRevisionService.ts`'s retention/delete) — this makes the deletion-vs-verification race structurally impossible rather than needing a separate comparison-against-surviving-records fix, closing both #338 items 3 and 4 with one mechanism. - Feature-detects `navigator.locks`; falls back to running the callback directly (today's behavior) with a one-time warning on runtimes that lack it. - Adds a minimal fair-mutex `navigator.locks` mock to `tests/setup.ts` (neither jsdom nor Node implement it) and fixes an incomplete `logger` mock in `dbServiceRetry.test.ts` that broke once the admission wrapper's `createLogger()` call entered its import chain. ## Test plan - [x] `tests/unit/storage/protectedWriteAdmission.test.ts` (new) — shared holders run concurrently, exclusive excludes/waits on shared and vice versa, result/error propagation, fallback when `navigator.locks` is absent. - [x] All directly-affected existing suites pass: `dbService*.test.ts`, `sceneRevisionService.test.ts`, `aiInferenceCacheService.test.ts`, `protectedStoreMigration.test.ts`, `tests/unit/services/storage/idb*.test.ts`. - [x] Broader sweep of every other test file mocking `services/logger` for a transitive break — only `dbServiceRetry.test.ts` needed the fix above. - [x] `pnpm run typecheck:single` clean. - [x] `pnpm run lint` clean. Part of the Phase 4 stack for #338; PR B (disable/rotate production flow, primary-store adapters, UI) is based on this branch. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by Sourcery Introduce a cross-tab admission mechanism to coordinate protected IndexedDB writes with encryption migrations, preventing races between key resolution, writes, and migration batches. New Features: - Add protectedWriteAdmission utilities that use the Web Locks API (or a safe fallback) to gate protected writers and migration batches via shared/exclusive admission locks. Bug Fixes: - Prevent protected writes from racing with active encryption migrations and landing data under superseded keys or generations. - Eliminate deletion-vs-verification races in cache eviction and scene revision retention that could produce false migration verification shortfalls. Enhancements: - Wrap all primary protected-store write and delete operations, as well as scene revision and inference cache durable writes, with the shared admission lock to ensure consistent coordination. - Limit migration batches to an exclusive admission lock per batch to balance writer safety with avoiding long-running writer starvation. - Add unit tests for the protected write/migration admission behavior and improve logger mocking to cover transitive imports. Tests: - Add dedicated tests for protectedWriteAdmission covering shared vs exclusive behavior, result/error propagation, and navigator.locks fallback. - Extend test setup with a minimal navigator.locks mock to support admission logic under jsdom/Node environments and adjust dbServiceRetry logger mocks to satisfy new dependencies. ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** Prevent encryption migrations from conflicting with protected storage updates ### What Changed - Protected saves and deletes now remain coordinated from encryption through database commit, preventing writes from using an outdated key or generation during migration. - Migration work pauses protected writers for one batch at a time, while allowing writers to continue between batches. - Scene revision saves, cache eviction, and retention cleanup now follow the same coordination rules, avoiding false migration verification failures. - Small unencrypted codex records are preserved correctly instead of being saved as empty data. - Older runtimes without Web Locks continue to operate with a direct-execution fallback and a warning. - Added coverage for concurrent writers, migration exclusion, fallback behavior, result propagation, and error handling. ### Impact `✅ Fewer encryption-migration write conflicts` `✅ No silent data loss for small codex records` `✅ Fewer false migration verification failures`

We check for security issues, mistakes in how you're setting up your infrastructure, and common code problems. We do this to make sure your changes are solid and won't cause any trouble later. ### Talking to CodeAnt AI Got a question or need a hand with something in your pull request? You can easily get in touch with CodeAnt AI right here. Just type the following in a comment on your pull request, and replace "Your question here" with whatever you want to ask:

This lets you have a chat with CodeAnt AI about your pull request, making it easier to understand and improve your code. #### Example

### Preserve Org Learnings with CodeAnt You can record team preferences so CodeAnt AI applies them in future reviews. Reply directly to the specific CodeAnt AI suggestion (in the same thread) and replace "Your feedback here" with your input:

This helps CodeAnt AI learn and adapt to your team's coding style and standards. #### Example

This tool helps you identify potential issues and areas for improvement in your codebase, ensuring your repository maintains high standards of code health.
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Reliability** * Improved coordination of protected data writes and encryption migrations across browser tabs. * Reduced conflicts during saves, deletions, cache updates, snapshots, project changes, and migrations. * Preserved existing retry, rollback, and error-handling behavior. * **Bug Fixes** * Added a safe fallback for environments without browser lock support. * Improved reliability when completing snapshot operations. * **Tests** * Expanded coverage for concurrent writes, migration ordering, failures, fallback behavior, and snapshot transactions.
